subject: general
question: Which specific chemical can be applied to achieve staining of chromosomes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Acetocarmine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Acetocarmine** is a widely used stain for chromosomes, particularly in cytogenetic studies.
 
• It is prepared by dissolving carmine in acetic acid, which enhances its ability to bind chromosomal material.
 
• This stain highlights chromosomes by binding strongly to their DNA and proteins, making them visible under a microscope.
 
• Acetocarmine is commonly used for studying mitosis and meiosis in plant and animal cells.
 
• Its application enables researchers to analyze chromosomal structure and behavior during cell division.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cytogenetics:** It is the study of chromosomes, their structure, and their function in relation to genetics.
 
• **Chromosome Staining:** Staining techniques, including acetocarmine and orcein, help visualize chromosomes for karyotyping and genetic analysis.
 
• **Mitosis and Meiosis:** These are fundamental processes of cell division where staining techniques play a critical role in observing chromosomal dynamics.
 
• **Carmine:** A natural dye extracted from cochineal insects, used to prepare acetocarmine and other biological stains.
 
• **Acetic Acid:** A vital component of acetocarmine, which aids in fixing and preserving cellular structures for microscopic examination.
